title: Part 1 pin probe result, format part1-pinprobe-v1 (one JSON object, last stdout line of libpart1_membw.so --pin-probe --json). Not a row.

gate_basis.description: cpuset_top_app, gate_off, cpuset_not_top_app, or none when the program stopped before the gate ran.

foreground_cpuset.description: The program's own /proc/self/cpuset as read; null when it could not be read.

status.description: ok: the probe ran (a CPU that did not pin is reported in cpus, it does not make the probe fail). skipped: the gate refused (exit 97). failed: usage error (2), timeout (124) or an error.

cpus.description: One entry per CPU probed, in the order of --cores. After a failure or a timeout: the CPUs completed before it.

result.description: ok: pin_retry pinned the thread and the spin saw the CPU all the time.

midr.description: MIDR_EL1 of this CPU as a hex string (engine 0.2.2 and later; optional, an object without it still validates). Read while the probe was pinned on that CPU: from sysfs cpu<n>/regs/identification/midr_el1, else assembled from this CPU's /proc/cpuinfo entry read during the spin (implementer, variant, part, revision; the architecture field is 0xf). For a CPU whose pin failed (engine 0.2.3 and later) the same two sources are read unpinned (midr_source sysfs_unpinned, cpuinfo_unpinned). null when no source gave it.

midr_source.description: Where `midr` came from: sysfs or cpuinfo (read while pinned on that CPU), sysfs_unpinned or cpuinfo_unpinned (engine 0.2.3 and later: the CPU's pin failed, so the same files were read without pinning), or null when midr is null.

reason.description: Refusal or error text; present when status is not ok.
